appeal_strategy_used: Resubmitted physician letter reiterating symptom severity; did not add conservative-treatment records.
notes: First recorded Meridian lumbar MRI denial. Denial letter specifically cited absence of documented conservative treatment prior to imaging. This is the case that establishes the pattern for HC-003/005/007.

appeal_strategy_used: Same approach as HC-001: resubmitted symptom narrative only.
notes: Repeat of HC-001's failure mode before the clinic changed its appeal approach.

appeal_strategy_used: Included documented conservative treatment (PT records) and a specialist referral in the appeal packet.
notes: First success after the clinic started including PT documentation. Basis for the emerging pattern.

appeal_strategy_used: Submitted partial PT records without noting the duration was short of Meridian's apparent threshold.
notes: PT documentation was present but only 2 weeks; denial letter reiterated a 6-week conservative-treatment expectation. Reinforces that duration, not just presence, of PT records matters.

appeal_strategy_used: Included extended PT records plus evidence of symptom progression despite conservative treatment.
notes: Strong replication of the HC-003 success pattern with additional progression evidence.

appeal_strategy_used: Appeal filed with symptom narrative only; billing staff was unaware of the emerging PT-documentation pattern.
notes: Preventable failure — pattern was already visible in HC-003/005 but wasn't applied to this case.

appeal_strategy_used: Deliberately replicated the HC-003/HC-005 strategy: PT records plus specialist referral.
notes: Confirms the pattern a third time. This is the case referenced in the 'memory strengthened' demo beat.

appeal_strategy_used: Submitted PT records alone, matching the usual successful pattern.
notes: PT documentation present (matches successful cases) but appeal still rejected — denial letter cited missing objective neurological exam findings. Shows the PT-documentation pattern is necessary but not always sufficient.

appeal_strategy_used: Resubmitted symptom narrative without lab results.
notes: Same insurer as the lumbar MRI cluster but a different procedure and denial reason. Should NOT surface when the agent is reasoning about lumbar MRI medical-necessity denials.

appeal_strategy_used: Obtained and submitted retroactive prior authorization from Meridian's utilization management department.
notes: Administrative fix, unrelated to the lumbar MRI clinical-evidence pattern. Different procedure, different denial reason.
Alliance Coastal Insurance, not Meridian. Surface pattern looks identical to the Meridian cluster (same procedure, same denial reason) but this is a different insurer with its own policy.

evidence_submitted: lumbar imaging dated 3 weeks before appeal filing
appeal_strategy_used: Included PT records and recent imaging in the same packet.
notes: Approved with PT records plus imaging dated well within 90 days of filing.

evidence_submitted: lumbar imaging dated 5 months before appeal filing
appeal_strategy_used: Included PT records, matching the pattern that works for Meridian.
notes: PT documentation present, matching the general pattern, but Alliance's denial letter separately cited imaging older than 90 days. Alliance appears to require recent imaging in addition to conservative treatment — a requirement not seen in the Meridian cluster. Do not assume Meridian's rule transfers directly to Alliance.

appeal_strategy_used: Submitted comprehensive clinical evidence package despite the denial reason being a coverage-policy classification rather than a documentation gap.
notes: Strong clinical evidence did not overturn the denial because Alliance classified the specific knee MRI protocol as experimental/investigational — a policy-level denial, not an evidence gap. More documentation would not have changed the outcome.

appeal_strategy_used: Symptom narrative only; appeal predates the clinic's current PT-documentation practice.
notes: Nearly 3 years old at time of writing. Meridian's medical policy may have changed since this case was resolved; treat as a weak, dated data point rather than current guidance.

appeal_strategy_used: Obtained retroactive authorization and included the original ordering justification.
notes: Only historical case on record for Summit Point Health Plans. Any pattern drawn from this alone should be flagged as a single data point, not an established trend.

appeal_strategy_used: Demonstrated to Meridian's claims department that the two submissions were a billing-system resubmission, not two separate visits, and requested reprocessing.
notes: Purely administrative resolution — no clinical evidence was relevant. Resolved in 15 days, the fastest turnaround in the case set.

evidence_missing: conservative treatment documentation specific to the knee
appeal_strategy_used: Appeal packet reused the lumbar-spine PT-documentation language without knee-specific conservative-treatment records.
notes: Same insurer and same general 'document conservative treatment' pattern as the lumbar MRI cluster, but for a different joint. The appeal failed because the submitted PT records were generic and not knee-specific — a caution against over-generalizing the lumbar pattern to any medical-necessity denial from this insurer.
